task_criteria: FAILIF: the trigger re-reads already-seen board events after restart or writes a runbook without operator approval; PROOF: uv run pytest tests/ -q (572 passed) including test_cursor_resume_falsifier_fails_without_persistence (memory-only cursor mutation replays events) and test_board_event_trail_flows_to_proposal_without_runbook_write (no runbook-tree writes), plus uv run lore validate exit 0

items.criterion: FAILIF: the trigger re-reads already-seen board events after restart or writes a runbook without operator approval; PROOF: uv run pytest tests/ -q (572 passed) including test_cursor_resume_falsifier_fails_without_persistence (memory-only cursor mutation replays events) and test_board_event_trail_flows_to_proposal_without_runbook_write (no runbook-tree writes), plus uv run lore validate exit 0
items.detail: Ran `uv run pytest tests/ -q` -> "572 passed in 3.83s" (exit 0); `uv run pytest tests/test_lore071_trigger.py -q` -> "6 passed"; `uv run lore validate` -> exit 0. No replay: lore/trigger.py:76-105 seeks to the persisted byte offset and advances the cursor only after the whole suffix parses; tests/test_lore071_trigger.py:17-56 proves 3 -> 1 -> 0 blocks across fresh store instances. No runbook write: lore/trigger.py's only write is the cursor file (JsonCursorStore.set, :44-63, atomic os.replace); the board is opened "rb" (:78); absorb_sweep/absorb_proposal/compiler.propose are data-only (grep for write/open in lore/absorb.py and lore/compiler.py returns docstrings only); tests/test_lore071_trigger.py:114-128 asserts the runbook tree is unchanged. Caveat recorded: test_cursor_resume_falsifier_fails_without_persistence (:58-76) is vacuous — it monkeypatches lore.trigger.JsonCursorStore, but consume() uses the injected instance (lore/trigger.py:77), so the mutation never takes effect and the test passes regardless; the persistence property is nonetheless proven by the resume test and by a live run (first consume 1 block, cursor file {"...events.jsonl": 76}, restart consume 0 blocks).

items.criterion: The persisted cursor survives a process restart so a new watcher instance does not replay already-consumed board events
items.detail: Live run: first consume -> 1 block, cursor file written {"/var/tmp/.../events.jsonl": 76}; second consume with a fresh JsonCursorStore -> 0 blocks. tests/test_lore071_trigger.py:17-56 asserts the same 3 -> 1 -> 0 sequence across new watcher/store instances.

items.criterion: The trigger layer has no runbook/board write path — only the cursor file is written
items.detail: lore/trigger.py:44-63 is the sole write (cursor JSON via temp file + os.replace); board opened read-only "rb" (:78); AugerDecisionTableAdapter.read only calls read_text (:218-220); lore/absorb.py and lore/compiler.py contain no write/open calls (grep hits are docstrings only). tests/test_lore071_trigger.py:114-128 asserts the runbook tree still contains only the operator-owned marker.

items.criterion: Cursor failure paths raise instead of silently replaying (corrupt store, offset past EOF)
items.detail: Live run: corrupt cursor -> ValueError "invalid cursor store ...: Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes"; offset past EOF -> ValueError "cursor offset 99999 is past board size 76; refusing replay" (lore/trigger.py:82-86, :38-42, :55-60).

items.criterion: The new trigger is reachable from a documented entrypoint (library API or CLI)
items.detail: Documented library API with a runnable snippet in docs/ABSORB-TRIGGER.md:37-51 and linked from README.md:467-468; no CLI subcommand exists (lore/__main__.py:794-1060), but the docs state explicitly that no timer/service is installed and an owner runs the watcher from a managed process — the task did not require a CLI.

items.criterion: The Auger adapter emits provenance (table + row id) and is read-only
items.detail: lore/trigger.py:180-192 sets source=f"auger:{table}:{row_id}" and fields {table,row_id,row}; tests/test_lore071_trigger.py:88-110 assert source "auger:decisions:D-001" and that the tmp tree is unchanged before/after — both pass in the 6-passed run.

findings.detection: new public symbol `parse_auger_export`/`AugerDecisionTableAdapter`/`BoardEventWatcher`/`JsonCursorStore` are exported but no CLI command, route, or config key registers them; only tests and docs reference them
findings.detail: `__all__` lists the four symbols and docs/ABSORB-TRIGGER.md shows manual usage, but no production caller (CLI, absorb entry point) imports `lore.trigger` — the feature is unwired outside tests.

findings.detection: failure paths of `JsonCursorStore.get`/`set` and `BoardEventWatcher.consume` (invalid cursor JSON, offset past EOF, malformed event line) have no tests
findings.detail: `get`/`set` raise ValueError on corrupt store and `consume` raises ValueError when `start > end` and on JSONDecodeError, but tests/test_lore071_trigger.py only exercises happy-path resume and the non-class-event skip.

findings.detection: `_board_event_block` accepts any non-`task_completed` event carrying `class_id`/`lesson`, contradicting the doc claim that only `task_completed` plus explicit-class records are accepted
findings.detail: The condition `if event_type != "task_completed" and not (detail.get("class_id") or detail.get("lesson") or event.get("class_id"))` lets `task_updated`/`audit` records through, and the fixture's `audit` record (id 3) is counted in the `len(first) == 3` assertion.

findings.detection: `_SECTION_NAMES` maps section titles to canonical names but `flush` compares `section in _SECTION_NAMES.values()` while `table = section`, so the mapping is redundant and the `break records`→`breaks` rename is never observable
findings.detail: `section = _SECTION_NAMES.get(title)` already stores the canonical value, making the `in _SECTION_NAMES.values()` guard and the separate `table` variable dead indirection.

findings.detection: `JsonCursorStore.set` re-reads and re-parses the store on every write and raises on any non-int value, but `get` silently defaults missing keys to 0 — asymmetric error handling for the same file
findings.detail: `get` returns `payload.get(str(board.resolve()), 0)` while `set` does `int(v)` for every entry and raises ValueError on a single bad value, so a store written by `get`-tolerant code can fail on `set`.
